title: Quarterly AML/CFT Awareness Test
summary: A short refresher and test that every employee repeats each quarter. It keeps the basics fresh between annual courses: what to watch for, when to escalate and what never to say to a customer.

lessons.title: Five-minute refresher
lessons.body:
## Before you take the test

Three habits protect you and the house:

- **Know the customer.** Identify who they are and why they are transacting, every time.
- **Notice the unusual.** Splitting amounts, rushed instructions, third parties waiting outside, documents that do not fit the story.
- **Escalate, do not investigate.** Report a concern to the Compliance Officer straight away and never tell the customer you have done so.

The test draws a few questions at random, so you may see different ones each quarter.

questions.prompt: A customer splits a large exchange into several smaller ones on the same day, each just under a reporting threshold. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Structuring is splitting transactions to stay under a threshold. Escalate it.

questions.prompt: If you suspect a transaction is suspicious, you should tell the customer so they can explain.
questions.explanation: Never tip off the customer. Report to the Compliance Officer instead.

questions.prompt: Who receives an internal report of a suspicion?
questions.explanation: Internal reports go to the Compliance Officer, who decides on any external report.

questions.prompt: Which of these are common red flags?
questions.explanation: A regular, consistent customer is not in itself a red flag.

options.label: A story that changes when you ask questions
A regular customer making their usual exchange
A third party giving instructions from outside

questions.prompt: What do we call the crime of warning a customer that a report has been made about them? (two words)
A customer who is in a hurry may skip identification this once.
questions.explanation: Identification is required every time, however busy the counter is.

questions.prompt: You spot a possible sanctions match for a customer. What do you do first?
questions.explanation: Pause and escalate. Do not complete the transaction.

questions.prompt: Why do we repeat this test every quarter?
questions.explanation: Regular reminders keep good habits strong between annual courses.

options.label: To keep the basics fresh and show staff stay alert
